title: Cave nightclub that did not pay and Mrs. Melanson's dances
summary: Nappy Lamar's booking pays almost nothing and Hazel needs a detective to retrieve his drums; another dance hostess keeps profits from homebrew.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Oh, it's down around, uh, nine, ten, eleven hundred, around there.
Is it near St. Peter or Orleans?
No, I think it's a little further down.

Around Dumain. I think it's down around there. I think they call it the cave now. Tony Fusio, I could tell you. Well, anyway, Nappy Lamar goes and books this job, you see. So, we go in there and we, we play all night long. And when we get through, the guy gives us fifteen cents and a pack of cigarettes. See. And, uh, what's that? Wasn't that? So, we went, we told him, uh-uh, we can't wait for that. See. So, he said, well, uh, I'll come back. It'll pick up. Business will pick up. It'll get better, you know. So, he wouldn't let me take my drums out. So, at the time, my daddy was in the District Attorney's office. He had the job like Johnny Grocer's got now, you know. He was chief investigator for the District Attorney's office. So, I had to call up the old man. I had to take a detective. Go down there and get my drums out. Cause the guy, he didn't want us to quit. He didn't want me to get my drums out. Yeah. It was a kick. And we played at another place.

back around where the Charlie Hospital is now. It used to be the parish prison, used to be right there in Saratoga and Tulane Avenue. There was an old lady used to give dances back there by the name of Melanson. They never had any electricity in us, just had these lanterns, you know, hanging around. And she'd give us a dollar, maybe a dollar and a half. And the first thing, we had a good band, and the first thing you know, man, the place is getting like that, you see. Well the more people would get in there, the more she'd serve homebrew, you know. Was doing probation, they'd serve homebrew. And the more people would put in there, the more she'd cry, but she's not making everything. We felt sorry for the poor old lady, you know. And she was putting the B on us left and right. So it finally took us about six or seven weeks to finally get smarter what she was doing to us, you know Bill. Oh, there's little incidents like that, that if you can only, if you can only think of.
